subject: Exchange: limited executive summary + redaction & NDA for penetration test
content:
From: Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@fintech.io>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: security+procurement@fintech.io
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: penetration test executive summary and remediation status

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement security review we need to review a high-level executive summary of your most recent third-party penetration test and a short remediation status update focused on critical/urgent items. We don’t need the full raw findings at this stage — a redacted exec summary that omits IP, target hostnames, and customer identifiers is fine.

Can you confirm:
- What level of redaction you can provide for an exec summary?
- Do you require an NDA before sharing anything?
- If yes, can you provide a limited-scope NDA we can sign?

We’re aiming to complete this step by EOD Friday (2026-12-18) to keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Luca Rossi
Head of Security, FinTech.IO

--

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@fintech.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test executive summary and remediation status

Hi Luca — appreciate the clear ask.

Short answers up front:
- We can provide an executive summary with targeted redaction that removes customer IDs, internal hostnames, and any PoC code.
- We do require a two-way limited NDA for the full redacted PDF; we can do a lighter shared exec summary without signatures if you only need a summary of findings and remediation percentages.

Plan options:
1) Quick path (no NDA signature): high-level one-page exec summary (no hostnames, no PoC, no appendices) — can send within 24 hours.
2) Standard path (recommended): sign our limited-scope NDA (only for PT artifacts) and we’ll provide a redacted PDF + redaction matrix and a short remediation tracker. Delivery within 48 hours of signature.

Laura (Legal Ops) — looping you for the NDA. Vanessa (Security Ops) — can you confirm the latest remediation % for critical/high items?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

--

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@fintech.io>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test executive summary and remediation status

Hi Luca,

Thanks — I can share a short limited-scope NDA for this specific artifact exchange. The NDA will: 
- Cover exchange of the redacted PT executive summary and supporting redaction matrix only.
- Prohibit further distribution to third parties.
- Expire 90 days after execution.

I’ll send a DocuSign link in a separate email (quick review, no edits recommended). If you need counterparty redlines we can review, but that will extend the timeline.

Laura Bennett
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

[Attachment stub: Redwood_Limited_PT_NDA_v1.docx]

--

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test executive summary and remediation status

Hi Luca — quick remediation snapshot:
- Critical (4): 3 remediated, 1 under monitoring (expected fix 2027-01-10).
- High (9): 7 remediated, 2 scheduled for code patch 2027-01-05.
- Overall closure rate for items classified as P1/P2: 78%.

I’ve attached the redaction matrix mapping which sections we will redact in the PDF (hostnames, specific PoC snippets, internal IP ranges). The redaction preserves findings and risk severity so you can evaluate risk posture without operational details.

[Attachment: redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx (Excel, 12 KB)]

If you sign the NDA, we’ll provide:
- PT_execsum_redacted_v0.2.pdf (exec summary w/ inline redaction markers)
- redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx (what we removed and why)
- remediation_tracker_link (read-only)

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Security Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Luca (on behalf of procurement)
